exercise1.prompt: Bringing two tables together on the column they share.

hiddenCases.name: the join keeps the left-hand rows

exercise1.hint: how="left" keeps every person. The people who matched nothing have a missing score, and isna().sum() counts them.

questions.prompt: What does the default inner merge keep?
choices: Only keys present in both tables
questions.explain: Rows whose key is missing on either side disappear. That is why an inner join can silently shrink your population.

questions.prompt: You want every person, with a score where one exists. Which join?
questions.explain: Left keeps the left table whole and fills gaps on the right, which is the shape of "my population, plus what I know about them".

questions.prompt: What should you check immediately after a merge?
questions.explain: Fewer rows means an inner join dropped some; more means the key was not unique and rows multiplied. Both are worth catching at once.
